title: Tensorial Neural Networks: Generalization of Neural Networks and Application to Model Compression
sections_checked: sequential versus end-to-end compression and convergence analysis
evidence_note: At 10% parameters on ResNet32/CIFAR10 in the table holding sequential compression fixed, TNN-mCP is 91.28% vs NN-CP 88.50%, TNN-mTK is 81.59% vs NN-TK 86.73%, and TNN-mTT is 87.89% vs NN-TT 87.08% (uncompressed 93.2%). Gains depend on tensor decomposition; parameter count is not measured latency/energy.

title: EasyQuant: Post-training Quantization via Scale Optimization
sections_checked: scale-search method and calibration sample protocol
RK3399 ARM runtime tables and limitations below seven bits
evidence_note: EasyQuant uses 50 calibration examples in its experiments vs 1,000 for the TensorRT comparison. INT7 ResNet50/ImageNet is 75.04% vs 75.20% FP32; MobileNet-SSD/VOC2007 is 68.79 mAP vs 72.04 FP32 (and above INT7 TRT 63.88). Measured INT7 ARM latency is lower than INT8 TRT on two RK3399 boards, e.g. SqueezeNet 44 vs 66ms and ResNet50 300 vs 415ms in a four-thread setting. Task/platform-specific result.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sections_checked: GLUE adaptation table and trainable-parameter counts
GPT-3 175B training throughput and shared-base storage estimate
evidence_note: RoBERTa-large/GLUE LoRA uses 0.8M trainable parameters with average score 89.0 vs full fine-tuning's 355M and 88.9; paper marks the full-fine-tune result as reported from prior work, not a matched rerun. GPT-3 175B throughput is 43.1 vs 32.5 tokens/s/GPU on V100. Shared base checkpoint remains necessary. No added inference latency assumes merging updates into base weights. Adapter alternatives add measurable online latency.

title: When Attention Collapses: How Degenerate Layers in LLMs Enable Smaller, Stronger Models
review_status: full-text section audit complete; publication chronology flagged
evidence_note: GPT-2 Medium 16-layer Inheritune scores 48.08 average on five listed tasks vs 47.74 for 24-layer full model and 46.84 for a 16-layer scratch model. Inheritune uses inherited weights from a larger pretrained checkpoint; 100K steps versus 200K for the same-width scratch baseline. This supports transfer/warm-start efficiency, not free compression independent of teacher pretraining. Scope centers on GPT-2/Pre-LN and particular initialization. Final v4/TMLR 2026 result must not be backdated to 2024.

title: MoE-Lens: Towards the Hardware Limit of High-Throughput MoE LLM Serving Under Resource Constraints
sections_checked: throughput and workload-specific results for MoE-Lightning/vLLM comparisons
offline batching scope and KV-cache/prompt-generation sensitivity
evidence_note: On one socket/GPU of a dual-socket Intel 8380/A40 server, reports 4.6x average throughput over MoE-Lightning. The 25.5x maximum belongs to RAG (19.4x mean); AIME reaches up to 9.9x (4.7x mean); Figure 11's overall MoE-Lightning comparison says maximum 12.4x. Target is offline/batched throughput, and gains vary with request lengths and KV cache size. Not a general latency or hardware-independent factor.

title: Quantization Degradation in Large Language Models: A Signal-Noise Perspective
sections_checked: de-randomized retention definition and main tables
source SNR and cross-layer propagation analyses
evidence_note: 76 weight-only PTQ configurations, five model families, four methods, four bit-widths and 11 benchmarks. W3 retention varies sharply: Llama2-7B RTN 60.0% vs SPQR 89.2%; Qwen3-0.6B GPTQ 30.6% vs Qwen3-14B 87.9%. Uses de-randomized retention, not raw accuracy, with finite task samples. Supports strong method/scale/task interactions, not universal performance loss at a bit width.
